reasons: Both answers give the same correct NOT EXISTS anti-join with a relative 90-day cutoff, only the given columns, and no remark about when to send or deliver a message, so all four rubric items are met on both sides. A: pg_stat_user_indexes reports index names and usage counters, not indexed columns, so it cannot show whether an existing index already covers the (customer_id, created_at) prefix; pg_indexes or \d orders is the correct check.
"whether it picks the anti-join or falls back to a hash anti-join over a full scan" is self-contradictory: a hash anti-join is an anti-join, so the stated alternatives are not alternatives.
B: "the planner treats it as an anti-join either way" is wrong for PostgreSQL: because of NOT IN's NULL semantics the planner does not convert NOT IN into an anti-join and evaluates it as a hashed SubPlan instead, which is a real performance difference and not just a NULL-safety one.
